llm_direct_judge.test_access: visible_context, candidate_action, and pre-execution evidence only

experiment_1.claim: recursive harness revisions improve ranking and fixed-budget scientific action selection within each task family
experiment_1.response: use regime-held-out test groups, independent feedback and acceptance sets, strong non-RHI learned baselines, fixed-coverage risk, AURC, fixed-budget utility, and five paired seeds
experiment_1.reviewer_challenge: a low selective risk may be produced by abstaining, a random split may leak regimes, or gains may come from a learned classifier rather than recursion
experiment_1.title: Experiment 1 — task-specific validity

experiment_2.claim: an action-worthiness contract learned on two task families transfers zero-shot to a third
experiment_2.response: exclude all target records from source training/calibration/acceptance, balance source tasks in loss and calibration, evaluate on held-out target regimes, and report a target-supervised upper bound
experiment_2.reviewer_challenge: target calibration leakage or task-size imbalance can manufacture transfer, and failure may simply reflect an impossible target
experiment_2.title: Experiment 2 — cross-task transfer

experiment_3.claim: one jointly trained harness remains stable across seeds and does not sacrifice a smaller task to optimize the largest dataset
experiment_3.response: use inverse-frequency task weighting, macro acceptance, apply exactly the same selected joint gate to every task slice, and report per-task and macro-over-task results
experiment_3.reviewer_challenge: pooled metrics are dominated by the 10,987-record unique-material task
experiment_3.title: Experiment 3 — joint robustness

experiment_4.claim: recursive checkpoint selection, rather than a single learned gate, improves the scientific action-worthiness decision
experiment_4.response: evaluate active H0, H1, H2, and H3 checkpoints on one untouched test split, compare guarded acceptance with always-accept mutation, and report paired change from H0 by task and policy
experiment_4.reviewer_challenge: an accepted revision may be selected by acceptance noise, or a final score may hide regressions across intermediate harness versions
experiment_4.title: Experiment 4 — self-evolution ablation

protocol.always_accept_policy: accept every schema-valid candidate without using test performance
protocol.guarded_policy: accept candidate only when the held-out acceptance gate selects candidate
protocol.test_selection: all H0-Hk checkpoints are evaluated on the untouched test split after selection; test is never used for acceptance

limitations: Historical outcomes are benchmark-derived offline action-worthiness proxies, not expert annotations or online MatBot trajectory outcomes.
The deterministic proposer is a reproducible trajectory-conditioned RHI implementation, not evidence that an LLM proposer improves the harness.
llm_direct_judge is an optional one-shot baseline: it sees only the visible action context and does not train, mutate a harness, or receive trajectory feedback.
Scientific utilities are reported per task and as macro summaries; pooled utility is not interpreted as a common physical unit.
Source train, feedback, and acceptance records are disjoint but can share source regimes; final test regimes remain group-disjoint.

split_policy.acceptance_role: RHI candidate H_i versus H_(i+1) model selection only
split_policy.feedback_role: trajectory failure diagnosis and threshold calibration
split_policy.historical: complete scientific regimes are held out for test; remaining records are disjointly assigned to train, feedback, and acceptance
split_policy.test_role: final reporting only; never used to propose or accept a harness
split_policy.transfer_role: held-out target task contributes no records to zero-shot training, feedback, calibration, or acceptance
